class.name: RectND
class.description: RectND is a class that represents an axis-aligned rectilinear box in N-dimensional space. It is the ND version of [Rect2], [AABB], Rect4, etc. Methods that combine a [RectND] with a point, a direction, or another [RectND] operate in the highest dimension of all of their inputs, with any missing elements treated as zero. This means a lower-dimensional [RectND] behaves like a flat slab that is zero-size in the axes it does not define, so for example a 2D [RectND] only contains points whose extra elements are all zero.

method.name: abs
method.description: Returns a new [RectND] with a positive size and the position adjusted accordingly.

method.name: continuous_collision_depth
method.description: Sweeps this [RectND] along [param relative_motion] and returns the fraction of that motion which can be traveled before hitting the [param obstacle] [RectND]. A return value of [code]1.0[/code] means the motion is unobstructed, while a smaller value means the motion is stopped partway through. Note: This function can return values outside of the expected range, including values above [code]1.0[/code], below [code]0.0[/code], and even below [code]-1.0[/code]. Negative values indicate depenetration, moving out of an obstacle this [RectND] already overlaps. Handling the meaning of such values is up to the caller. For the expected use case of looping over many obstacles, start with a ratio of [code]1.0[/code] and take the minimum of the ratio and the result on each loop iteration. The calculation is performed in the highest dimension of this [RectND], [param relative_motion], and [param obstacle], with any missing elements treated as zero.

method.name: continuous_collision_overlaps
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if sweeping this [RectND] along [param relative_motion] overlaps the [param obstacle] [RectND] at any point during the motion. This is a cheaper check than [method continuous_collision_depth] for when only the yes-or-no answer is needed, such as for broad-phase collision culling. The calculation is performed in the highest dimension of this [RectND], [param relative_motion], and [param obstacle], with any missing elements treated as zero.

method.name: duplicate
method.description: Returns a copy or clone of the [RectND]. The underlying data uses Godot's Vector type, which is copy-on-write, so this is a cheap operation if the transform is not modified.

method.name: encloses_exclusive
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] encloses the other RectND, but not if they only share a border.

method.name: encloses_inclusive
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] encloses the other RectND, including if they share a border.

method.name: expand_self_to_point
method.description: Expands the [RectND] to include the given point.

method.name: expand_to_point
method.description: Returns a new [RectND] expanded to include the given point.

method.name: from_center_size
method.description: Constructs a [RectND] from a center position and a size. The size is the "diameter" of the rect, not the "radius".

method.name: from_position_end
method.description: Constructs a [RectND] from a start position and an end position.

method.name: from_position_size
method.description: Constructs a [RectND] from a start position and a size.

method.name: get_nearest_point
method.description: Returns the point in the [RectND] closest to the given point.

method.name: get_space
method.description: Returns the space of the [RectND] (area, volume, hypervolume, etc) by multiplying the size of each dimension.

method.name: get_support_point
method.description: Returns the point in the [RectND] that is the farthest in the given direction.

method.name: get_surface
method.description: Returns the surface of the [RectND] on the boundary by multiplying all combinations of all-but-one dimension and adding them up.

method.name: grow
method.description: Returns a new [RectND] grown by the given amount in all directions.

method.name: has_any_size
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if any element of [member size] is non-zero, including negative elements. Compare with [method has_surface], which only considers positive elements.

method.name: has_point
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] contains the given point.

method.name: has_space
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if every element of [member size] is positive, meaning [method get_space] is positive. A rect that is flat in even one dimension has no space, so this returns [code]false[/code] for it.

method.name: has_surface
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if any element of [member size] is positive. Compare with [method has_any_size], which also counts negative elements.

method.name: intersection
method.description: Returns a new [RectND] that is the intersection of this [RectND] and the other RectND.

method.name: intersects_exclusive
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] intersects the [param other] [RectND], but not if they only share a border.

method.name: intersects_inclusive
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] intersects the [param other] [RectND], including if they share a border.

method.name: is_equal_approx
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this [RectND] and [param other] are approximately equal, by running [method @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx] on each component.

method.name: is_finite
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [RectND] is finite, by running [method VectorND.is_finite] on the position and size vectors.

method.name: merge
method.description: Returns a new [RectND] that encloses both this [RectND] and the [param other] [RectND].

method.name: raycast_intersects_dict
method.description: Performs a raycast against the rect. The [param from] parameter is the starting point of the ray, and the [param direction] parameter is the direction of the ray, which must be normalized. A hit is only reported if it is closer than [param max_distance], which is exclusive. If [param inside_is_zero] is [code]true[/code] and [param from] is inside the rect, the ray immediately hits at a distance of zero with a zero normal, instead of casting forward to the surface it would exit through. The returned [Dictionary] may contain the following keys: - [code]"hit"[/code]: A boolean indicating whether the ray hit any part of the rect. - [code]"distance"[/code]: The distance from the starting point to the hit point. - [code]"normal"[/code]: The normal at the hit point, perpendicular to the surface. - [code]"point"[/code]: The point of intersection. This is the same as [code]from + direction * distance[/code]. If the ray does not hit any part of the rect, the returned dictionary will be [code]{"hit": false}[/code]. The calculation is performed in the highest dimension of this [RectND], [param from], and [param direction], with any missing elements treated as zero.

members.member: The "center" position of the rect. This value is calculated by adding [member position] and half of [member size], and is not stored internally. When setting this value, [member position] is adjusted accordingly, and the rect keeps the same [member size].
The dimension of the rect. This is the dimension of the position and size vectors. The position and size vectors must have the same dimension or the rect is invalid.

The "end" position of the rect, in the positive direction. This value is calculated by adding [member position] and [member size], and is not stored internally. When setting this value, [member size] is adjusted accordingly, and the rect keeps the same [member position].
The "start" position of the rect, in the negative direction. This value is stored internally as a VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]).
The size of the rect. Valid values are positive numbers. This value is stored internally as a VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]).
